definition: A graph of stars' luminosity, on the vertical axis, against their surface temperature, on the horizontal axis with temperature decreasing to the right; stars group into regions such as the main sequence, giants and white dwarfs.

A massive star late in its life, with a luminosity of roughly $10^{4}$ to $10^{6}$ times the Sun's and a radius up to about a thousand times the Sun's; supergiants lie across the top of the HR diagram.
The apparent shift of a nearby star against much more distant stars as the Earth orbits the Sun; the parallax angle, half the shift seen six months apart, gives the star's distance.
The distance at which 1 AU subtends an angle of 1 arc-second, so a star with parallax angle $p$ in arc-seconds is $d = \frac{1}{p}$ parsecs away; 1 pc is 3.26 light years.
